sources.title: University of South Africa: Northern Sotho language introduction
sources.note: Direct university course text read. Related Northern Sotho dialects, Southern Sotho and Tswana; no population percentages or current official-language counts reused.

sources.title: Nthabiseng Mokoena, Thaba-Bosiu: a historical archaeological study (2024)
sources.note: Full 267-page dissertation downloaded from university bitstream 5ab0d167-e6d3-48f0-bdff-f331a25bfd00 and text extracted locally. Printed pp. 190 to 192, 217 to 221 inspected. Counts of enclosures are internally inconsistent and not reused; no certain bead workshop claimed.

sources.title: Eugène Casalis, The Basutos (1861), household observations
sources.note: Full public-domain original OCR read and saved. Printed pp. 137 to 145: grass granary construction, grinding, meal and evening-star names. Missionary account uses prejudiced comparisons; examples are attributed rather than presented as universal timeless customs.

sources.title: Morija Museum: Arbousset’s 1840 journey with Moshoeshoe
sources.note: Direct museum book catalogue read. Missionary Excursion into the Blue Mountains, 1991 edition of the account of the 1840 journey; museum précis explicitly describes Moshoeshoe’s enthusiasm for literacy as a means of uniting his people.

sources.title: Saffron Walden Museum: Southern Africa, object 52
sources.note: Direct full eight-page object guide read. Human PDF page 2, object 52: springbok-ear rattles made before 1841, worn by Sotho men for dances. Same URL has 145 words in the preceding Nguni card; combined budget must include it.

sources.title: Daniel P. Kunene, Leselinyana la Lesotho and Sotho Historiography (1977)
sources.note: Direct original article extract and notes read, not paywalled full paper. DOI 10.2307/3171582. Extract preserves Mogaogeli oa Moetsalibe and translates The Sinner’s Pardoner; note 4 explicitly retains original orthography. First issue 3 November 1863; interruptions 1865 to 1869 and 1880 to 1881.

sources.title: Cape of Good Hope, Basutoland Annexation Act No. 12 (1871)
sources.note: Indexed original statutory text, printed p. 178 preamble, read; direct PDF fetch failed. Act dated 11 August 1871. Racist civilizational justification for special administration and legislation is paraphrased critically; no claim that passage of the act was the operative proclamation date.

sources.title: Library of Congress: Basutoland map and historical description
sources.note: Full indexed original catalogue description read after direct fetch failed. Map dated approximately the 1870s. Historical description: Moshoeshoe’s consolidation in the 1820s and 1830s, protection 1868, Cape annexation 1871, separate colonial rule 1884, independence 4 October 1966.

sources.title: Edward A. Alpers, Muqdisho in the Nineteenth Century: A Regional Perspective (1983)
sources.note: Direct original article extract and references read. Urban revival, Indian merchant capital at Zanzibar, enslavement and agricultural production, town quarters and Omani/Italian intervention. Full paywalled paper not claimed read.

sources.title: Nicholas W. S. Smith, The machinations of the Majerteen Sultans (2015)
sources.note: Original research article abstract read at author repository and indexed publisher DOI 10.1080/17531055.2014.970602. Rulers Uthman Mahmud Yusuf and Yusuf Ali, piracy and protection treaties interpreted as political strategy, not lack of political institutions.

sources.title: S. B. Miles, report on the African coast near Bunder Murayah, Transactions XIX (1868 to 1873)
sources.note: Indexed original archival OCR read at printed pp. 147 and 153. Related page 147 URL ends 0x00003d; both pages are ONE work charged together. Hunda mat manufacture, portable houses, seasonal entrances; defined frankincense plots. Modern botanical validity of repeated tapping claim not adopted. Direct page fetches failed; indexed text was available.

sources.title: Richard F. Burton, First Footsteps in East Africa (1856)
sources.note: Direct public-domain transcription read. Chapter V describes Del and Wesi in western Somali travel context beyond imported polygon. Appendix I summarizes Speke’s 1854 observations around Las Kuray: well and guano exports. Prejudiced colonial conclusions are not adopted; observations explicitly attributed.

sources.title: Smithsonian National Museum of African Art, Benaadir cloth 2013-2-16
sources.note: Full indexed original museum record read after direct fetch failed. Somali Hawiye or Digil artist, Mogadishu, 1969 to 1971; orange cloth with blue stripes. Historical label traces nineteenth-century response to American factory cloth through local cotton cultivation. Alternate si.edu object URL is same work.

sources.title: Virginia Luling, The Social Structure of a Southern Somali Tribe (1971)
sources.note: Full 376-page public UCL dissertation downloaded and text extracted. Printed pp. 74 to 76 historical cloth and coffee discussion distinguished from later fieldwork; pp. 194 to 195 and 202 colonial chronology. Geledi/Afgooye lies outside imported polygon and is explicitly contextual. Thesis historical chronology has some later Jubaland simplifications not reused.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Imported polygon lies in Nigeria, wholly outside the southern African subject. Public overview warns explicitly. No association with Lesotho/Basutoland cards; narrower Basotho narrative stated, broad Sotho label preserved.

Historical regional record, not modern Somalia or modern Somaliland. No aliases. Outline omits Mogadishu itself at approximately 2.05 N, as well as Geledi and western Somali areas; public overview and site passages identify wider regional examples. Named Benaadir examples are regional context, not proof the outline is correct.
